summary: Describes the RTP payload format for JPEG video, optimized for real-time streams in which the codec settings rarely change between frames. It was replaced by RFC 2435.

eli5.summary: A movie made of pictures is cut up into packets and numbered so it can be streamed across a network.

questions: rtp payload format for jpeg video
how to stream jpeg over rtp
subtitle: How to send JPEG video frame-by-frame over real-time networks.

tldr.problem: JPEG is a still-image compression standard, but video can be compressed by treating each frame as an independent JPEG image. Getting these compressed video frames to arrive in order and on time over packet networks requires special handling.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 2035 defines a packet format where a 64-bit RTP/JPEG header carries quantization settings, image dimensions, and fragment offsets, allowing hardware codecs to decode frames without needing the full JPEG table specifications in every packet.
tldr.outcome: JPEG video could be streamed over RTP with efficiency and resilience to packet loss, but this RFC was superseded by RFC 2435 with clarifications.

today: RFC 2035 was a Proposed Standard and has been obsoleted by RFC 2435, which clarifies the original specification.

sections.title: JPEG Compression and Motion-JPEG
sections.content:
JPEG (the Joint Photographic Experts Group standard) defines compression algorithms for still images. Video can be compressed in a technique called Motion-JPEG by compressing each video frame independently as a JPEG image and transmitting them in sequence. The JPEG standard supports four modes of operation: sequential DCT, progressive DCT, lossless, and hierarchical, each subdividing images into frames and scans with various compression parameters.

JPEG uses table-based compression with quantization tables and Huffman coding tables that are defined in headers within the compressed stream. However, in practice, most hardware JPEG video codecs implement only the sequential DCT mode with a single interleaved scan in YUV color space, and these compression parameters rarely change from frame to frame within a single video stream.
sections.eli5: JPEG squeezes pictures by throwing away details your eyes can't see. Compression tables tell the decoder how much detail to throw away. For video, the same tables usually work for many frames in a row.

sections.title: RTP/JPEG Header and Packet Format
sections.content:
Because JPEG compression parameters remain constant across many frames, RFC 2035 uses an abbreviated format where the tables are omitted from the transmitted JPEG data. Instead, a 64-bit RTP/JPEG header is placed between the RTP header and the JPEG scan. This header contains eight fields. The Type field specifies which quantization and Huffman tables are in use; six type codes are predefined with different chroma sampling factors. Types 0 and 2 and 4 use 4:2:2 chroma subsampling (horizontal only), while types 1, 3, and 5 use 4:2:0 (both horizontal and vertical). The three pairs differ in whether restart markers are present and how they align with packet boundaries.

The Q field encodes the quantization tables; for values 1 through 99, a formula scales the standard JPEG quantization tables. Width and Height fields encode the image dimensions in 8-pixel multiples (so a width of 40 means 320 pixels). The Fragment Offset is the byte offset of the current packet within the JPEG scan, and the RTP timestamp appears across all fragments of a single frame.
sections.eli5: Each packet has a small header saying what kind of compression was used, how much detail to keep, how big the picture is, and where this piece of the picture goes. All packets from the same picture have the same timestamp.

sections.title: Fragmentation and Restart Markers
sections.content:
JPEG frames are often larger than the maximum packet size, so they must be fragmented across multiple RTP packets. The RTP marker bit is set in the last packet of a frame, and each packet carries the Fragment Offset so that the receiver can detect missing packets and reassemble frames efficiently even when packets arrive out of order.

To aid recovery from packet loss, RFC 2035 defines three pairs of type codes based on whether restart markers are present. Type 0/1 have no restart markers and place no restrictions on fragmentation. Types 2/3 include restart markers (via a DRI segment) but still allow arbitrary fragmentation. Types 4/5 align restart intervals with packet boundaries, allowing decoders to partially decode frames by processing one restart interval at a time. The Type-specific field carries a restart count (RCOUNT) starting at zero and incrementing for each restart interval, with special values 254 and 255 marking continuation and final packets of a restart interval.
sections.eli5: When a big picture is split into packets, each packet says where it belongs (its offset in the data). The last packet gets a special marker. For better recovery from lost packets, the picture can be divided into restart intervals that align with packet boundaries, and each interval can be decoded on its own.

sections.title: Quantization and Sampling
sections.content:
Six RTP/JPEG type codes are predefined, corresponding to baseline DCT sequential mode, 8-bit samples, square pixels, three components (Y, U, V) in the YUV color space, and standard Huffman tables from the JPEG specification. The Y component (luminance) uses Huffman table 0 and quantization table 0, while U and V components (chrominance) use Huffman table 1 and quantization table 1.

The odd types (1, 3, 5) employ 4:2:0 chroma subsampling, downsampling chrominance both horizontally and vertically by 2, which is the most common video format. The even types (0, 2, 4) use 4:2:2, downsampling chrominance horizontally by 2 only. Additional types in the range 128-255 may be defined dynamically by session setup protocols.
sections.eli5: JPEG lets you throw away different amounts of color detail for the eyes to barely notice. 4:2:0 means color is a quarter resolution; 4:2:2 means color is half resolution horizontally. These sampling factors and quantization tables can be referenced by a single type number instead of being included in every packet.

sections.title: Algorithmic Quantization
sections.content:
For Q values from 1 to 99, the quantization tables are computed algorithmically using a scale factor derived from the Q field. The scale factor is calculated as S = 5000 / Q for Q from 1 to 50, and S = 200 - 2*Q for Q from 51 to 99. This value then scales the standard JPEG quantization tables (tables K.1 and K.2 from the JPEG specification), with each value saturated to 8 bits.

For Q values of 0 or 100 and above, fixed or dynamically defined quantization tables are used. Q = 0 is reserved. This approach allows a video sender to adjust the quality level of the stream in real time simply by changing the Q value sent in the RTP/JPEG header, enabling rate-adaptive transmission or user-controlled quality adjustment.
sections.eli5: The Q number is like a quality dial: higher Q means better quality, lower Q means smaller file sizes. From 1 to 99, a formula turns Q into multiplication factors for the standard compression tables. Very high Q uses special tables.

fields.desc: Byte offset of the current packet in the JPEG scan.

fields.desc: Specifies quantization and Huffman tables, sampling factors.
